## Overview

This note models monthly Pakistan solar panel prices (log scale) against global
polysilicon prices (log scale), January 2017 to May 2026 (n = 113). Because panel
prices in Pakistan are largely a function of an imported input, the analysis treats
polysilicon as an exogenous driver rather than modelling panel price in isolation,
and checks whether the two series are cointegrated before forecasting.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
pkgs <- c("forecast", "tseries", "urca", "lmtest", "ggplot2")
invisible(lapply(pkgs, function(p) if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages(p, repos = "https://cran.r-project.org")))
library(forecast); library(tseries); library(urca); library(lmtest); library(ggplot2)

brand_green <- "#2C5F2D"
brand_brown <- "#8B7355"
```
:::


## Data preparation


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
df <- read.csv(params$data_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
df$Date <- as.Date(df$Date, format = "%d/%m/%Y")
df <- df[order(df$Date), ]
stopifnot(!anyNA(df$log_commodity_price), !anyNA(df$log_polysilicon))

y <- ts(df$log_commodity_price, start = c(2017, 1), frequency = 12)  # panel price (log)
x <- ts(df$log_polysilicon,     start = c(2017, 1), frequency = 12)  # polysilicon price (log)

knitr::kable(head(df, 6), caption = "First six observations")
```

## Stationarity tests

Both series look non-stationary in levels. The battery below runs ADF, KPSS, and
Phillips-Perron on levels and first differences.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
unit_root_battery <- function(series, name) {
  cat("\n===", name, "===\n")
  cat("ADF (level):  p =", round(adf.test(series)$p.value, 4), "\n")
  cat("KPSS (level): p =", round(kpss.test(series, "Level")$p.value, 4), "\n")
  cat("PP  (level):  p =", round(pp.test(series)$p.value, 4), "\n")
  cat("ADF (1st diff): p =", round(adf.test(diff(series))$p.value, 4), "\n")
}
unit_root_battery(y, "Log Panel Price")
```

## Cointegration


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
eg_reg <- lm(y ~ x)
summary(eg_reg)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

-0.47923 -0.23939 -0.01016  0.21182  0.52348
```

:::

```{.r .cell-code}
eg_resid <- residuals(eg_reg)
eg_adf <- ur.df(eg_resid, type = "none", selectlags = "AIC")
cat("\nEngle-Granger step 2 (residual ADF), tau =", round(eg_adf@teststat[1], 3),
    " | 5% crit =", eg_adf@cval[1, "5pct"], "\n")
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Sample-size caveat
With n = 113 monthly observations, the Johansen and Engle-Granger tests have
limited power. Read the cointegration result as indicative and re-estimate as
more months of data accrue.
:::

## Model estimation and out-of-sample accuracy

The last 13 months are held out; ARIMA, ARIMAX, and a naive random-walk
benchmark are compared on RMSE, MAE, and MAPE.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
train_h  <- 100
y_train  <- window(y, end = time(y)[train_h])
x_train  <- window(x, end = time(x)[train_h])
y_test   <- window(y, start = time(y)[train_h + 1])
x_test   <- window(x, start = time(x)[train_h + 1])

m_arima  <- auto.arima(y_train, stepwise = FALSE, approximation = FALSE)
m_arimax <- auto.arima(y_train, xreg = x_train, stepwise = FALSE, approximation = FALSE)

summary(m_arima)
```

```{.r .cell-code}
  ARIMA  = accuracy(f_arima,  y_test)["Test set", c("RMSE", "MAE", "MAPE")],
  ARIMAX = accuracy(f_arimax, y_test)["Test set", c("RMSE", "MAE", "MAPE")],
  Naive  = accuracy(f_naive,  y_test)["Test set", c("RMSE", "MAE", "MAPE")]
```

## Final model and 12-month forecast


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
final_arimax <- auto.arima(y, xreg = x, stepwise = FALSE, approximation = FALSE)
final_x_ar   <- auto.arima(x)
x_future     <- forecast(final_x_ar, h = 12)$mean

fc_trend <- forecast(final_arimax, xreg = x_future, h = 12)
fc_flat  <- forecast(final_arimax, xreg = rep(tail(x, 1), 12), h = 12)

autoplot(fc_trend) +
  labs(subtitle = "xreg = ARIMA-projected polysilicon price", y = "log(panel price)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Policy relevance

::: {.callout-important}
## Policy relevance

- **Pass-through**: the cointegrating regression implies a 1% rise in global
  polysilicon price is associated with roughly a
  0.48% long-run change in Pakistan panel prices.
- **Direction of influence**: the Granger results point to the global
  polysilicon market driving domestic panel prices rather than the reverse,
  consistent with Pakistan being a price-taker with negligible domestic module
  manufacturing.
- **Forecast signal**: the 12-month projection points to a
  continued decline in log panel prices, which is supportive of further
  residential and commercial solar uptake so long as duty and tax structures
  on imported modules are not tightened.
- **Levers with real traction**: since pricing is driven by an imported input
  with no domestic hedge, the policy options with the most bite are
  (a) tariff/GST rationalization on panels and inverters, (b) exchange-rate
  pass-through management, and (c) incentives for local cell/module assembly
  to reduce exposure to polysilicon price cycles.
:::
